clue.text: Incentive for a bishop in bed

indicators.note: the bishop and the letter a are set in the middle of the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
RR is Right Reverend, the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what reward would tempt a bishop lying in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A and RR inside COT. The carrot as a reward comes from the carrot dangled in front of a donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrot is a reward offered to tempt someone, as opposed to the stick of punishment.

clue.text: He died in drink and named church supporting poor sister

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece that supports another sits below it in the grid

parts.note: the Poor Clares are an order of nuns, so a poor sister is a Clare
N is an abbreviation for named
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A tale of a man who drank himself to death and the church that props up a poor nun.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supporting' puts N and CE below CLARE. The Duke of Clarence in Shakespeare's Richard III is drowned in a cask of malmsey wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Duke of Clarence is murdered by being drowned in a butt of malmsey, a sweet wine.

clue.text: Sneering wickedly about Germany's flag

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the abbreviation for Germany
wickedly suggests the letters of the word before it are twisted out of shape

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: Someone sneers nastily at the German national flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wickedly' makes an anagram of SNEERING, and 'about' puts it around D, giving RED ENSIGN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Ensign is the flag flown by British merchant ships.

clue.text: Free a lovebird?

parts.note: love is a score of nil in tennis, the letter O
a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: A question about letting a pet lovebird loose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lovebird' splits into 'love' and 'bird'. The 'a' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Open as an adjective means unrestricted or available to all, like free.

clue.text: Tries the altered garment

indicators.note: the letters of the two words before it are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tries on a garment that has been altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altered' makes an anagram of TRIES THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tee shirt is a casual top worn on the upper body, so it is an item of clothing.

clue.text: Identity of a trainee in trade union

indicators.note: the letter a and the trainee are placed inside the trade union

parts.note: Equity is the British actors' trade union
L stands for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A question of how a new apprentice fits within a workers' union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A and L inside EQUITY. Equity is the trade union for actors in Britain; L is the learner plate on a British learner driver's car.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics an identity is an equation true for all values, an expression of sameness.

clue.text: Deputy seaman usually found on watch

parts.note: a second is an assistant or deputy, as in a duel
a hand is a crew member on a ship

explanation.surface: A deputy sailor is generally the one on watch duty on deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'watch' suggests a sailor's shift on deck; here it is a wristwatch.
explanation.definitionFit: The thin pointer that sweeps round the dial of a timepiece counting seconds is usually present.

clue.text: Unable to succeed in record time

parts.note: an EP is an extended play record

explanation.surface: Someone fails to make a record in the time allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone inept is clumsy and lacking in skill, so tends to fail.

clue.text: Temporary accommodation housed an occupier

indicators.note: the temporary shelter holds the next piece within it

parts.note: a tent is a temporary shelter

explanation.surface: A temporary shelter gave a home to someone living there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housed' puts AN inside TENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenant is someone who occupies a property rented from a landlord.

clue.text: Teacher losing maiden's flower

indicators.note: the teacher drops the letter for a maiden

parts.note: a master is a schoolteacher
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A teacher loses a girl's favourite bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes M out of MASTER. In cricket a maiden is an over with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: The aster is a daisy-like garden plant with star-shaped blooms.

clue.text: Apply oneself to hoarding clothing

parts.note: a hoarding is a billboard, which carries an ad
dress means clothing

explanation.surface: Someone concentrates on stockpiling clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hoarding' looks like stockpiling; it is the British word for a billboard, which displays an advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: To address a task is to set about tackling it with effort.

clue.text: Bob loses your article? That's disgusting!

parts.note: the saying Bob's your uncle, with the word your taken away, makes Bob the same as a father's brother
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone named Bob mislays your item, and the speaker is repelled.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'Bob's your uncle' (meaning 'and there you are') minus 'your' says Bob is UNCLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclean means dirty or impure, so something unclean can be revolting.

clue.text: A bird hides in the wilderness

indicators.note: the bird's letters are tucked away inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: A bird conceals itself out in the wild.
explanation.definitionFit: The erne is the sea eagle, a large bird of prey.

clue.text: Running towards Norway's capital

parts.note: welling means flowing or running, as tears well up
to means towards
N is the international vehicle code for Norway

explanation.surface: Someone is dashing to reach Oslo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Norway's capital' looks like a phrase for Oslo or a first letter; Norway gives N and 'capital' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Wellington is the capital city of New Zealand.

clue.text: It fastens to a line and clips on the nuts

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters of the words before it are scrambled

explanation.surface: Something grips a washing line and snips the nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' makes an anagram of CLIPS ON THE. A clothes-pin is the American word for a clothes peg.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothes-pin is a peg that holds wet laundry on a washing line.

clue.text: Sharp prominence in Cyprus

indicators.note: the raised ground is placed inside the code for Cyprus

parts.note: CY is the international vehicle code for Cyprus
a hill is a prominence, a raised piece of land

explanation.surface: A steep hill stands out on Cyprus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts HILL inside CY.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp weather is biting cold, as a chilly wind is.

clue.text: Inquisitive and tense, absorbed in the Book of Changes

indicators.note: the tense letter is soaked up inside the ancient Chinese text

parts.note: the I Ching is the Chinese Book of Changes
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Someone curious and nervous is engrossed in an ancient Chinese text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbed in' puts T inside I CHING.
explanation.definitionFit: Itching to know means eager and curious about something.

clue.text: Eye problem leaves listeners in the dark

indicators.note: the listeners are placed within the dark

parts.note: night is the dark
ears are the organs we listen with

explanation.surface: A vision disorder means people listening are left unable to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts EARS inside NIGHT; 'leaves' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Short-sightedness, where distant objects are blurred, is a defect of vision.

clue.text: Beast's nut or butt

parts.note: a hog is a pig, a beast
nut is slang for head

explanation.surface: A list of an animal's body parts: head or rear end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butt' looks like a backside; here it is a large barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A butt is a large cask, and a hogshead is a large cask too.

clue.text: Thanks after veteran brought about end of feud

indicators.note: the thanks come after the veteran in the answer
the veteran is put around the following word

parts.note: end as written
ta is British slang for thanks

explanation.surface: Gratitude after an old soldier helped end a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought about' puts VET around END, and 'after' puts TA at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a long-running blood quarrel between families.

clue.text: Fulsomeness gets agreement out of court

indicators.note: the agreement sits outside the court, enclosing it

parts.note: union means agreement or harmony

explanation.surface: Excessive flattery secures a settlement without going to trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of court' suggests a settlement; here 'out of' puts UNION outside CT.
explanation.definitionFit: Unction is an excessive, oily earnestness, the quality of fulsome praise.

clue.text: The resident I meant is transformed

indicators.note: the letters of the two words before are transformed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone clarifies which resident they had in mind, now changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is transformed' makes an anagram of I MEANT.
explanation.definitionFit: An inmate is someone living in an institution such as a prison or asylum.

clue.text: Work on stand for double-dealer

indicators.note: in a down clue the work sits on top of the stand

parts.note: W is the symbol for work in physics
an easel is a stand for a painting

explanation.surface: Someone working on a painting stand is a cheat.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts W above EASEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A weasel is a sly, treacherous person, so a double-dealer.

clue.text: Intrepid poet

explanation.surface: A brave writer of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Hardy wrote poems as well as novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardy means bold and robust; Thomas Hardy was an English poet and novelist.

clue.text: Formulate a method for rapid travel in the US

definitions.text: for rapid travel in the US

parts.note: to express is to put into words, to formulate
a way is a method

explanation.surface: Someone works out a plan for fast transport in America.
explanation.definitionFit: An expressway is an American divided highway built for fast traffic.

clue.text: Puritanical about a legendary king

indicators.note: the prudish word goes around the letter a

parts.note: prim means prudish or puritanical

explanation.surface: A prudish story about an ancient ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts PRIM around A.
explanation.definitionFit: Priam was king of Troy during the Trojan War in Greek legend.

clue.text: Applied thought after losing masthead

indicators.note: the word loses its top letter, as a mast loses its head

parts.note: mused means thought or pondered

explanation.surface: A sailor's idea after a ship's mast top is lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after losing masthead' drops the first letter of MUSED.
explanation.definitionFit: Used means put to work, applied to a purpose.

clue.text: 25's wife loses high explosive in the country

indicators.note: the queen's name drops the letters for high explosive

parts.note: Hecuba was the wife of Priam, the answer to 25

explanation.surface: A queen gives up her explosives once in the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' takes HE from HECUBA.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuba is an island nation in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Dotty painting results after artist's fifth drink

indicators.note: the fifth letter of the word artist is picked out

parts.note: a tipple is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: An artist's fifth glass produces a wobbly picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dotty' looks like crazy; here it means made of dots.
explanation.definitionFit: Stippling is painting or drawing with small dots.

clue.text: Largely comatose model found on the floor

indicators.note: largely means most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: drugged means stupefied, comatose
the Model T was a Ford car

explanation.surface: A model is discovered lying unconscious on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Largely' drops the last D from DRUGGED; the Model T Ford gives T.
explanation.definitionFit: Drugget is coarse woven fabric used as a rug or floor covering.

clue.text: Drink made Noel tipsy

indicators.note: tipsy means drunk and unsteady, so the letters before it stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A Christmas drink made someone called Noel tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipsy' makes an anagram of MADE NOEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemonade is a soft drink flavoured with lemons.

clue.text: Ray hides posh dress

indicators.note: the fish conceals the letter for posh within it

parts.note: a manta is a large ray
U means upper class, posh

explanation.surface: Someone called Ray keeps an expensive frock out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hides' puts U inside MANTA. U for upper class is a British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantua was a loose gown worn by women in the 17th and 18th centuries.
